name: Alpha-lipoic acid

lead: Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA) is a sulfur-containing cofactor for mitochondrial enzymes and a redox-active antioxidant, available as a supplement and in some skincare products.
Its best-established human use is symptom relief in diabetic neuropathy. Claims for skin and anti-aging benefits rest on thin evidence.

paras: ALA and its reduced form dihydrolipoic acid scavenge reactive oxygen species and regenerate other antioxidants, and may influence insulin signaling and NF-κB activity.
Generally well tolerated; nausea, rash and, rarely, hypoglycemia in people on glucose-lowering drugs can occur. Legal as a supplement.
